lines: A nice stick can be many things if nobody important is watching.
I carried an empty bucket all morning. Very light work. Very confusing.
I once put bread in a chest and called it planning. Nobody argued.
There is a story from the village square, but it sounds smaller unless you were there.
Once I followed a chicken and found three missing buttons and no explanation.
A cloud looked like a loaf of bread, and then I was hungry all afternoon.
I tried to count fence posts and discovered one was avoiding responsibility.
The bell rang once while I was upside down. It sounded more official that way.
A trader asked me for directions and somehow both of us got less certain.
I once guarded a puddle from stepping feet until the sun stole it.
A child gave me a pebble for safekeeping. I still take the duty seriously.
There was a day when everyone looked busy and I found the missing bucket.
I sat near the well and heard the echo agree with me. Rare support.
A door opened by itself once. Wind got the credit, but I remain thoughtful.
I followed my own footprints in mud and learned I walk strangely when thinking.
A golem stared at a flower for a long time, so I did too.
I once invented a game and forgot the rules before losing.
The square was empty one morning and still somehow felt crowded with chores.
I found a stick shaped like a question and carried it until it answered nothing.
